'''Austin James Rivers''' (born August 1, 1992) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who is currently a [[sports analyst]] for [[ESPN]] and [[NBC Sports]]. The son of basketball coach and former player [[Doc Rivers]], he played for 11 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). In the [[2012 NBA draft]], Rivers was selected with the 10th overall pick by the [[New Orleans Hornets]] (now Pelicans), playing three seasons there before being traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. After three years with the Clippers, he was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in June 2018. In December of the same year, he joined the [[Houston Rockets]]. He also played in the NBA for the [[New York Knicks]], [[Denver Nuggets]], and [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].

Rivers led [[Winter Park High School]] to back-to-back Florida 6A state championships in 2010 and 2011. He also played in the 2011 [[Nike Hoop Summit]] for Team USA, and was a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]]. He was one of the top rated high school basketball players in the class of 2011, being rated as high as No. 1 by Rivals.com. In October 2010, Rivers committed to [[Duke University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Rivers, 2011 Shooting Guard, Duke |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/athletes/austin-rivers-14624?view=pv |access-date=June 12, 2025 |website=Rivals.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

On January 16, 2015, Rivers became the first player in NBA history to play for his father, coach Doc Rivers, then-head coach of the Clippers.

==High school career==
In 2010, Rivers led [[Winter Park High School]] to the school's first state title in a 76–57 win against [[Dr. Phillips High School]] in the 6A state championship. Rivers scored 23 points in the game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.theledger.com/article/20100306/news/3065036?p=1&tc=pg |title=Rivers Leads Winter Park to Title |publisher=TheLedger.com |date=March 6, 2010 |access-date=August 28, 2010}}</ref> In June 2010, Rivers was a part of the gold medal-winning team at the FIBA Americas U18 Championship where he set a Team USA record for an U18 event with 35 points against Canada.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2010/writers/luke_winn/07/02/rivers.notes/index.html |title=Austin Rivers impressed many with his performance at FIBA tourney |magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=July 2, 2010 |access-date=August 24, 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100824113114/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2010/writers/luke_winn/07/02/rivers.notes/index.html| archive-date= August 24, 2010 | url-status= dead}}</ref> On August 5, 2010, Rivers was named to the fifth annual [[Boost Mobile]] Elite 24 game,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/high-school-wire/2010/08/elite-24-roster-revealed-first-12/ |title=Elite 24 Roster Revealed (First 12) |publisher=Slam Online |date=August 5, 2010 |access-date=August 28, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100806080459/http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/high-school-wire/2010/08/elite-24-roster-revealed-first-12/ |archive-date=August 6, 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref> where he was named co-MVP after he had 25 points, 4 rebounds and 4 assists.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/basketball/os-hs-austin-rivers-elite-24-20100828,0,7416783.story |title=Austin Rivers is named co-MVP at ESPN all-star event |publisher=OrlandoSentinel.com |date=August 28, 2010 }}</ref>

On September 30, 2010, Rivers committed to [[Duke University]]. His commitment was widely covered by ESPN and various other sports networks given his status as the Class of 2011's top recruit.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/news/story?id=5632647 |title=Austin Rivers commits to Duke |work=ESPN.com |date=September 30, 2010 |access-date=March 29, 2023}}</ref> He officially signed with the program on November 16, 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=205032031 |title=Duke Inks Four During Early Signing Period |work=GoDuke.com |date=November 16, 2010 |access-date=November 19, 2014}}</ref>

On March 5, 2011, Rivers led Winter Park to back to back Florida 6A state championships with a 52–44 victory over [[Dr. Phillips High School]], in which he had 25 points, 11 rebounds and 4 steals.<ref>{{cite web|author=Collings, Buddy |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2011/03/05/winter-park-repeats-as-6a-champ-with-win-over-dr-phillips/ |title=Winter Park repeats as 6A champ with win over Dr. Phillips |work=Orlando Sentinel |date=March 5, 2011 |access-date=March 22, 2011}}</ref> Rivers was named the 2011 [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year]] on March 10, 2011.<ref>{{cite web |author=Payne |first=Greg |date=March 11, 2011 |title=Austin Rivers earns national honor |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/celtics/post/_/id/4681563 |access-date=March 29, 2023 |publisher=ESPNBoston.com}}</ref> He was also an All-American and All-State honoree, and played in the 2011 Nike Hoop Summit for Team USA.

==College career==
[[File:Austin Rivers warmup.jpg|thumb|right|Rivers with the Blue Devils in 2011]]
As a freshman, Rivers played in Duke's exhibition games in China and Dubai during an international tour in August 2011. In the first game against the [[China men's national basketball team]], Rivers scored 18 points on 8–19 shooting and led Duke to a 77–64 victory. In the second game (also against the Chinese national team), Rivers scored 12 points in a 78–66 victory, making several dunks during the first half. In the final game played in Beijing, Rivers chipped in 11 points as Duke topped the Chinese, 93–78.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Duke Tops China, 93-78, Sweeps Series|url=https://goduke.com/news/2011/8/22/205245948.aspx|access-date=2020-11-22|website=Duke University|language=en}}</ref> In his team's 86–66 victory over the Dubai national team, he scored 16 points, including 10 in the second quarter, on an array of impressive drives.

On February 8, 2012, his three-point basket as time expired allowed Duke to overcome an 82–72 deficit with two minutes to play in an 85–84 victory over the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Austin Rivers Game-Winning Shot vs. UNC (2012)|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JlIhh7yYcBo |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/JlIhh7yYcBo |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live|work=YouTube.com|access-date=March 8, 2016|date=February 8, 2016}}{{cbignore}}</ref> The victory ended North Carolina's 31-game winning streak at the [[Dean Smith Center]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=320390153 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201028210611/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=320390153 |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 28, 2020 |title=Austin Rivers' 3-pointer caps Duke rally, stuns North Carolina |work=ESPN.com |date=February 28, 2012 |access-date=November 19, 2014}}</ref>

On March 16, 2012, Rivers' college career ended in the "Round of 64" of the NCAA tournament, when Duke lost to [[Lehigh University]]. Rivers shot 5-of-14 from the field, while playing 34 minutes. Lehigh led for most of the game, earning their first NCAA Tournament victory.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2012-03-17|title=Rapid Reaction: Lehigh 75, Duke 70|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/54382|access-date=2020-11-22|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref>

On March 26, 2012, Rivers declared for the [[NBA draft]], foregoing his final three years of college eligibility.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rivers Officially Declares For NBA Draft|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2012/03/rivers-officially-declares-for-nba-draft.html|access-date=2020-11-22|website=Hoops Rumors|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===New Orleans Hornets / Pelicans (2012–2015)===
[[file:Austin Rivers Pelicans Summer League 2013.jpg|left|thumb|Rivers with the Pelicans during the [[NBA Summer League]] 2013]]
Rivers was selected by the New Orleans Hornets with the 10th overall pick the [[2012 NBA draft]]. Rivers chose to wear the #25 jersey, the same number his father wore when he was in the NBA. The night before the draft, Rivers said, "I want to be like my dad, only better." Joining him as a rookie on the Hornets was [[Anthony Davis]], the first overall pick of the draft. On July 24, 2012, Rivers signed his rookie scale contract with the Hornets.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/07/24/hornets-davis-rivers.ap/ |title=Rookies Davis, Rivers sign contracts with Hornets |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=November 19, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150131060342/http://www.nba.com/2012/news/07/24/hornets-davis-rivers.ap/ |archive-date=January 31, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Three days later, Rivers underwent successful surgery to clean up bone spurs in his right ankle.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Austin Rivers Undergoes Successful Surgery|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/austin-rivers-undergoes-successful-surgery|access-date=2020-11-22|website=New Orleans Pelicans|language=en}}</ref>

On October 31, 2012, Rivers made his NBA debut in the Hornets' season opener against the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. In 24 minutes as a starter, he scored 7 points on 1-of-9 shooting in a 99–95 loss.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20121031/SASNOH/gameinfo.html Notebook: Spurs 99, Hornets 95]</ref> On December 14, he scored a then career-high 27 points in a 113–102 loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20121214/MINNOH/gameinfo.html Notebook: Timberwolves 113, Hornets 102]</ref> On March 6, 2013, he broke his hand and subsequently required surgery that forced him to miss the remainder of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rivers Has Successful Surgery|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/rivers-has-successful-surgery|access-date=2020-11-22|website=New Orleans Pelicans|language=en}}</ref> For his rookie season, he averaged 6.2 points on 37% shooting from the field and 33% from three-point range. In April 2013, the Hornets changed their name to the Pelicans.

On October 16, 2013, the Pelicans exercised their third-year team option on Rivers' rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the [[2014–15 NBA season|2014–15 season]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pelicans Exercise Third-Year Options on Anthony Davis and Austin Rivers|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-exercise-third-year-options-anthony-davis-and-austin-rivers|access-date=2020-11-22|website=New Orleans Pelicans|language=en}}</ref> On April 12, 2014, Rivers recorded season highs in points and rebounds with 20 and 10, respectively, in the Pelicans' 111–104 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20140412/NOPHOU/gameinfo.html Notebook: Rockets 111, Pelicans 104]</ref>

On October 24, 2014, the Pelicans declined to exercise their fourth-year team option on Rivers' rookie scale contract, thereby not extending the contract through the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Reid|first=John|title=Pelicans pick up fourth-year option on Anthony Davis' contract, but not Austin Rivers'|url=https://www.nola.com/sports/pelicans/article_8a113dc9-ddf2-56fe-b5d8-89cf273996d8.html|access-date=2020-11-22|website=NOLA.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Pelicans Decline Fourth-Year Option On Austin Rivers|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/235316/Pelicans-Decline-Fourth-Year-Option-On-Austin-Rivers|access-date=2020-11-22|website=basketball.realgm.com}}</ref> On December 20, 2014, he scored a season-high 21 points in a 114–88 loss to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20141220/PORNOP/gameinfo.html Aldridge leads Trail Blazers over Pelicans 114-88]</ref>

===Los Angeles Clippers (2015–2018)===
[[File:Austin Rivers (31585856272).jpg|thumb|right|Rivers goes for a [[layup]] in 2016]]
On January 12, 2015, Rivers was traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] in a three-team trade involving the Pelicans and the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Boston Celtics Complete Three-Team Trade|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/boston-celtics-complete-three-team-trade|access-date=2020-11-22|website=Boston Celtics|language=en}}</ref> Three days later, he joined [[Doc Rivers|his father]] on the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] after he was traded in a three-team trade involving the Celtics and the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=LOS ANGELES CLIPPERS ACQUIRE AUSTIN RIVERS IN THREE-TEAM TRADE|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/clippers-acquire-austin-rivers-three-team-trade|access-date=2020-11-22|website=Los Angeles Clippers|language=en}}</ref> On January 16, Rivers made his debut for the Clippers and became the [[List of second-generation National Basketball Association players|first son to play for his father]] in an NBA game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150116/CLELAC/gameinfo.html |title=Irving scores 37, Cavaliers hold on to beat Clippers 126-121|work=NBA.com|date=January 16, 2015|access-date=January 16, 2015}}</ref> On February 21, Rivers scored a then-career-high 28 points in a 129–98 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150221/SACLAC/gameinfo.html | title=Redick's 24 points help Clippers blow out Kings 126-99 | work=NBA.com | date=February 21, 2015 | access-date=February 22, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161025094834/http://www.nba.com/games/20150221/SACLAC/gameinfo.html | archive-date=October 25, 2016 | url-status=dead }}</ref> On May 8, he scored a playoff career-high 25 points in the Clippers' 124–99 victory that gave them a 2–1 lead in the Western Conference semi-finals against the Houston Rockets.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150508/HOULAC/gameinfo.html | title=Austin Rivers propels Clippers past Rockets 124-99 | work=NBA.com | date=May 8, 2015 | access-date=May 9, 2015}}</ref>

On July 13, 2015, Rivers re-signed with the Clippers.<ref>{{cite news|title=CLIPPERS SIGN AUSTIN RIVERS AND COLE ALDRICH|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/clippers-sign-austin-rivers-and-cole-aldrich|access-date=July 13, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2015}}</ref> On February 6, 2016, he was ruled out for four to six weeks with a broken left hand.<ref>{{cite news|title=Clippers' Austin Rivers has been diagnosed with...|url=https://twitter.com/WindhorstESPN/status/696180551191887872|access-date=February 6, 2016|work=Twitter|date=February 6, 2016}}</ref> On March 31, he scored a career-high 32 points in a 119–117 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Adams' late basket lifts Thunder past Clippers 119-117|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160331/LACOKC/gameinfo.html|access-date=April 1, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=March 31, 2016}}</ref> On April 29, Rivers recorded 21 points and eight assists against the Portland Trail Blazers in game 6 of their first-round playoff series. However, with a 106–103 loss, the Clippers were eliminated from the playoffs. In the game, Rivers required 11 stitches above his left eye from a collision in the first quarter.<ref>{{cite news|title=Blazers advance 4-2 with 106-103 victory over the Clippers|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160429/LACPOR/gameinfo.html|access-date=May 2, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=April 29, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160430043121/http://www.nba.com/games/20160429/LACPOR/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 30, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On July 8, 2016, Rivers again re-signed with the Clippers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-re-sign-free-agents-crawford-johnson-mbah-moute-and-rivers|title=Press Release: Clippers Re-sign Free Agents Crawford, Johnson, Mbah A Moute And Rivers|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2016|access-date=July 8, 2016}}</ref> On December 14, 2016, he scored a season-high 25 points on 7-of-10 from three-point range and 9-of-12 from the field in a 113–108 win over the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899818|title=Clippers hold off Magic 113-108 for third straight win|work=ESPN.com|date=December 14, 2016|access-date=December 14, 2016}}</ref> On January 4, 2017, he set a new season high with 28 points in a 115–106 win over the Memphis Grizzlies.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899954|title=Clippers rally behind Rivers to beat Grizzlies 115-106|work=ESPN.com|date=January 4, 2017|access-date=January 5, 2017}}</ref> He averaged career highs of 12.0 points, 2.2 rebounds and 2.8 assists during the 2016–17 regular season, but due to a strained left hamstring, Rivers missed the last six games of the regular season and the first four games of the playoffs before returning in game 5 of the Clippers' first-round playoff series against the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2017/04/24/austin-rivers-return-los-angeles-clippers-game-5|title=Austin Rivers to return for Los Angeles Clippers in Game 5|work=NBA.com|date=April 24, 2017|access-date=April 25, 2017}}</ref>

On December 3, 2017, Rivers scored a season-high 30 points in a 112–106 loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975087|title=Butler scores 33 points, T-Wolves outlast Clippers 112-106|work=ESPN.com|date=December 3, 2017|access-date=December 4, 2017}}</ref> On December 22, 2017, he scored 30 of his career-high 36 points in the second half of the Clippers' 128–118 win over the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975226|title=Career night by Rivers leads Clippers over Rockets 128-118|work=ESPN.com|date=December 22, 2017|access-date=December 23, 2017}}</ref> The following night, he set a new career high with 38 points in a 115–112 loss to the Memphis Grizzlies.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975238|title=Evans, Gasol help Grizzlies defeat Clippers 115-112|work=ESPN.com|date=December 23, 2017|access-date=December 23, 2017}}</ref> Rivers missed 18 games between late December and early February with a heel bruise.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/clippers-austin-rivers-will-play-friday/|title=Clippers' Austin Rivers: Will play Friday|work=cbssports.com|date=February 9, 2018|access-date=February 9, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/clippers-austin-rivers-starting-at-point-guard-friday/|title=Clippers' Austin Rivers: Starting at point guard Friday|work=cbssports.com|date=February 9, 2018|access-date=February 9, 2018}}</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2018)===
On June 26, 2018, Rivers was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in exchange for [[Marcin Gortat]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Rosen|first=Zach|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-add-backcourt-trade-rivers|title=Wizards boost backcourt with Rivers trade|work=NBA.com|date=June 26, 2018|access-date=June 26, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Wojnarowski|first=Adrian|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23918159 |title=Clippers send Austin Rivers to Wizards for Marcin Gortat|work=ESPN.com|date=June 26, 2018|access-date=June 26, 2018}}</ref> On December 17, 2018, Rivers was traded with [[Kelly Oubre Jr.]] to the [[Phoenix Suns]] for [[Trevor Ariza]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/phoenix-suns-complete-trade-washington-wizards|title=Phoenix Suns Complete Trade with Washington Wizards|work=NBA.com|date=December 17, 2018|access-date=December 17, 2018}}</ref> Rivers was waived by the Suns the following day.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/phoenix-suns-waive-austin-rivers |title=Phoenix Suns Waive Austin Rivers |work=NBA.com |date=December 18, 2018}}</ref>

===Houston Rockets (2018–2020)===
[[File:Austin Rivers shooting.jpg|alt=Man shooting a basketball|thumb|Austin Rivers shooting]]
On December 24, 2018, Rivers signed with the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-free-agent-austin-rivers|title=Rockets Sign Free Agent Austin Rivers|work=NBA.com|date=December 24, 2018|access-date=December 24, 2018}}</ref> On January 5, 2019, he scored a season-high 21 points in a 110–101 loss to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071258|title=Trail Blazers beat Rockets as Harden's 40-point streak ends|work=ESPN.com|date=January 5, 2019|access-date=January 6, 2019}}</ref> On April 7, in a 149–113 blowout win against the [[Phoenix Suns]], Rivers made the 27th three-pointer of the game with 1:09 left on the clock in the fourth quarter, beating the Rockets' own previous record of most made threes by one team in a game (26).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.red94.net/houston-rockets-149-phoenix-suns-111-new-records-set-in-blowout/17189/|title=Houston Rockets 149, Phoenix Suns 111: New records set in blowout|last=McGuire|first=Paul|date=2019-04-07|website=Red94|language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/game?gameId=401071874|title=Suns vs. Rockets - Game Summary - April 7, 2019 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=2019-04-13}}</ref> He appeared in 47 games while averaging 8.7 points, 2.3 assists and 1.9 rebounds in 28.6 minutes per game. The Rockets won 72% of their games after signing Rivers. He started 13 straight games as a Rocket from December 31 through January 25, averaging 11.6 points, 3.8 assists and 2.7 rebounds in 38.1 minutes per game. Houston was 15–5 when Rivers scored in double figures and 9–1 when he recorded at least four assists. He also had nearly as many steals (29) as turnovers (32) with the Rockets.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-re-sign-austin-rivers|title=Rockets Re-Sign Austin Rivers|website=Houston Rockets|language=en|access-date=2019-07-17}}</ref> On August 9, 2020, Rivers scored a career-high 41 points off the bench and the Rockets used a big third quarter to pull away and cruise to a 129–112 victory over the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the [[2020 NBA Bubble|Orlando bubble]]. Rivers made six 3-pointers as Houston improved to 4–1 at Disney on a night the Rockets played a second straight game without [[Russell Westbrook]], who had a bruised right [[quadriceps]].<ref>{{cite news| url = https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/nba/rivers-has-career-high-41-as-rockets-down-kings-129-112/2020/08/09/4b79c5e2-dab2-11ea-b4f1-25b762cdbbf4_story.html| title = Rivers has career-high 41 as Rockets down Kings 129-112 - The Washington Post| newspaper = [[The Washington Post]]}}</ref>

===New York Knicks (2020–2021)===
On November 27, 2020, Rivers was acquired by the [[New York Knicks]] via a sign-and-trade deal that sent the draft rights of [[Issuf Sanon]] to Houston.<ref>{{cite web|title=Knicks Sign Austin Rivers|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-sign-austin-rivers|website=NBA.com|date=November 27, 2020|access-date=November 27, 2020}}</ref> On March 25, 2021, Rivers was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in a three team trade<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Acquires Tony Bradley, Austin Rivers, Two Second-Round Draft Picks and Generates Trade Exception|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/acquisitions-210325|date=March 25, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=March 25, 2021}}</ref> that sent [[Terrance Ferguson]], [[Vincent Poirier]], the drafts rights of [[Emir Preldžić]], and two future second-round picks to New York. Rivers was waived by the Thunder three days later.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Thunder Waives Austin Rivers|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-rivers-210328|date=March 28, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=April 16, 2021}}</ref>

===Denver Nuggets (2021–2022)===
On April 20, 2021, the [[Denver Nuggets]] signed Rivers to a 10-day contract<ref>{{cite web|title=Denver Nuggets Sign Austin Rivers to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-austin-rivers-042021|date=April 20, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=April 20, 2021}}</ref> following a season ending injury sustained by [[Jamal Murray]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Nuggets' Murray has torn ACL, out indefinitely|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31249220 |date=April 13, 2021|website=ESPN.com|access-date=April 20, 2021}}</ref> Ten days later, he was signed for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Denver Nuggets sign Austin Rivers|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/austin-rivers-signed-20210430|date=April 30, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=April 30, 2021}}</ref>

On September 1, 2021, Rivers re-signed with the Nuggets.<ref>{{cite web|title=Denver Nuggets Re-Sign Austin Rivers|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-rivers-090121|website=NBA.com|date=September 1, 2021|access-date=September 1, 2021}}</ref>

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2022–2023)===
On July 14, 2022, Rivers signed a one-year contract with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Free agent Austin Rivers agrees to 1-year deal with Minnesota Timberwolves|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34245485|website=ESPN.com|date=July 15, 2021|access-date=July 15, 2022}}</ref> On February 4, 2023, Rivers was suspended by the NBA for three games without pay due to his role in an altercation during a game against the [[Orlando Magic]] the day before. During the altercation, Rivers threw punches at Magic center [[Mo Bamba]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=NBA Communications on Twitter: "The following was released by the NBA." |url=https://twitter.com/NBAPR/status/1622063768959127552 |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=Twitter}}</ref>

== Broadcasting career ==
On October 23, 2023, it was announced that Rivers was hired by [[ESPN]] as an [[Sports analyst|NBA analyst]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-23 |title=11-Year NBA Veteran Reportedly Joining ESPN 
|url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/news/11-year-nba-veteran-reportedly-joining-espn-austin-rivers-timberwolves |access-date=2025-01-11 |website=Fastbreak On SI |language=en-US}}</ref>

Rivers joined [[NBC Sports]] for its [[College Basketball on NBC Sports|college basketball]] and [[NBA on NBC Sports|NBA]] coverage in 2025.<ref>{{cite news|last=Lerner|first=Drew|url=https://awfulannouncing.com/nbc/austin-rivers-hired-college-basketball-analyst.html|title=NBC Sports hires Austin Rivers as college hoops analyst|website=[[Awful Announcing]]|date=February 10, 2025|access-date=October 10, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nbcuniversal.com/article/nbc-sports-finalizes-game-analyst-team-and-adds-final-play-play-voice-nba-coverage-beginning-fall|title=NBC Sports Finalizes Game Analyst Team and Adds Final Play-By-Play Voice for NBA Coverage Beginning This Fall|work=[[NBCUniversal]]|date=July 24, 2025|access-date=October 10, 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Rivers was born in Santa Monica, California, the son of former [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] head coach and former player [[Doc Rivers]] and Kristen Rivers (née Campion).<ref>{{cite news|url=http://content.usatoday.com/communities/campusrivalry/post/2010/07/dad-says-austin-rivers-to-slow-it-down-and-wait-on-recruiting-trail/1 |title=Dad says Austin Rivers 'to slow it down and wait' on recruiting trail |work=USA Today |date=July 28, 2010 |access-date=August 24, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://select.nytimes.com/gst/abstract.html?res=F00610F838580C7B8EDDA80894DB494D81 |title=Moving Is Just Part of the Game Plan |first=Lena |last=Williams |date=January 28, 1993 |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] }}</ref> Doc Rivers was a former player who had joined the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] the summer of his son's birth. His older brother, [[Jeremiah Rivers|Jeremiah]], played basketball for [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]] and [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] and later joined the [[Maine Red Claws]], while his older sister Callie played [[Florida Gators women's volleyball|volleyball]] for the [[University of Florida]] and is married to his former Duke teammate and current [[Golden State Warriors]] player [[Seth Curry]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Dowd |first1=Katie |title=Seth Curry and Callie Rivers wed in Malibu ceremony|url=https://www.sfgate.com/warriors/article/Seth-Curry-wife-Callie-Rivers-carter-wedding-14441144.php|website=SFGate |access-date=15 September 2019 |language=en |date=14 September 2019}}</ref> His younger brother, Spencer, was a guard who played for [[UC Irvine Anteaters men's basketball|UC Irvine]] from 2014 to 2019.{{citation needed|date=April 2025}}

He was named Austin after former [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] guard [[Austin Carr]], while his middle name, James, is in honor of his great-uncle [[Jim Brewer (basketball)|Jim Brewer]].<ref name=carr>{{cite news|url=http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2013/03/austin_rivers_austin_carr_now.html | last=Schmitt Boyer|first=Mary|title=Austin Rivers, Austin Carr now old buddies: Cleveland Cavaliers Insider|access-date=April 1, 2013|newspaper=[[The Plain Dealer]]|date=March 31, 2013}}</ref>

His first child, a son with Brittany Hotard, was born in 2018. Rivers' two children with Audreyana Michelle, a son and a daughter, were born in March 2021 and June 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/knicks-austin-rivers-out-thursday/|title= Knicks' Austin Rivers: Out Thursday|work=CBS Sports|date=March 18, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/audreyanamichelle/p/C8uif7xOzMv/|title=Reese Rivers 🌸🤍🥹 06-21-24|work=Instagram|date=June 27, 2024}}</ref>
